A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PRO-DYN study, and their main text, equations, figures, and tables are readable. However, v1 ends after its references and lacks the Appendices A–F it cites, whereas v2 includes Appendices A–H. This limits comparison of the earlier supplementary material.

before.justification: Section 4 and Figures 3–6 report original forecasting experiments and ablations on modified models across 25 TFB datasets.

after.justification: Section 4 retains original forecasting experiments, with detailed scores, statistical comparisons, and prediction examples in Appendices G–H. Appendix F identifies one assumed PatchTST result separately.

M1.justification: The seven forecasting-model modifications remain unchanged. The PRO-DYN classification procedure is refined: v2 excludes paired non-learnable invertible transformations, changing NLinear from a pre-processing-plus-DYN configuration to DYN-only in Table 1. This revises the analytical framework rather than the forecasting architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate forecasting on the same 25 TFB datasets. V2's dataset inventory and prediction examples document retained coverage; its discussion of foundation and dynamics-based models does not introduce evaluations on additional tasks or datasets.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparisons retain the same seven model families, their vanilla versions, the applicable PRO controls, and NLinear as the reference. Additional models in v2's Appendix D are classified conceptually, not added as experimentally evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The stated common design retains MSE/MAE, 200 scores per model, original architecture hyperparameters, manually adjusted learning hyperparameters, and conditioning on horizon versus context length. V2 discloses splits, selection procedures, outlier thresholds, and missing-case handling without establishing that these settings changed.

E4.justification: The parameter-addition controls and horizon/context ablations match between v1's Figures 5–6 and v2's Figure 5. V2 also supplies outlier-inclusive comparisons, further conditioned results, and prediction cases, but v1 already references these analyses in its unavailable appendices. Their precise addition or revision cannot be established.

E5.justification: V1's visible figures indicate whether comparisons meet the significance threshold; v2 additionally provides metric-specific numerical p-values in Tables 14–18. Both retain one-sided Wilcoxon tests at 0.05. Neither supplies repeated-run counts, seed variability, or confidence intervals, so this is expanded reporting rather than evidence of additional runs.

E6.justification: V2 makes extensive per-dataset and per-horizon scores available in Tables 7–13, beyond the aggregate results visible in the supplied v1. Matched summaries also change: FiLM's normalized vanilla/DYN means move from -0.032/0.007 in v1 Figure 4 to -0.036/0.006 in v2 Figure 7 and Table 3. The main win/loss percentages remain unchanged. This substantially expands documented results without establishing new experimental runs.

T1.justification: V1's direct identification of linear-layer parameters with dynamics is replaced by definitions of discrete time-delay systems, the assumption L >= K, and a matrix-power argument treating LTSF-Linear as a relaxed dynamical system. Appendices B–C provide the longer-horizon derivation and discretization examples. These are substantive mathematical additions, although Section 3.2's last-row selection is inconsistent with Definition 3.3's descending state ordering.

C1.justification: The two central claims—benefits of learnable dynamics and placing the dynamics block last—remain. V2 explicitly restricts the empirical conclusions to single-dataset pattern-based models and qualifies the linear-model connection as a relaxed dynamical-system interpretation. The plug-and-play framing does not establish a new forecasting method.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands the qualifications and mechanism discussion. It explicitly recognizes bias from unequal horizon/context group sizes, changes FiLM's explanation from parameter addition plus data-length variation to parameter addition, and explains differing responses through temporal processing. Appendix D distinguishes architecture conclusions across model families, while Appendices F–G disclose the assumed PatchTST case and Informer's outlier-sensitive gain/loss finding.

D1.justification: Compared with v1's broad settings and unavailable appendix references, v2 supplies dataset splits, context lengths, optimizer and learning-rate details, software versions, hardware, and training times. Appendix F also describes model selection, supplementary code organization, the leaderboard snapshot used, and the unrun PatchTST configuration. These are substantial additions to reproducibility documentation, not demonstrated changes to the experiments.

R1.justification: V2 introduces a three-family research taxonomy and replaces the related-work discussion centered on known physical dynamics with broader Koopman, Takens, state-space, and diffusion positioning. Appendix D substantially extends the model analysis to foundation and dynamics-based approaches, including Chronos, Toto, Koopa, and SpaceTime. This goes well beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are rewritten, the introduction is reorganized around model families, and Section 3 receives extensive definitional and explanatory rewriting. Section 4.3 becomes a restructured performance-driver analysis. V2 also adds impact, LLM-use, and reproducibility statements and organizes the supplementary material into eight appendices.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the framework and architecture diagrams, adds an RQ2 schematic and configuration summary, and redesigns Table 1. V1's normalized-performance scatter plot moves to the appendix while Table 3 summarizes its means; the two conditioned-result figures are merged and annotated with group frequencies. Extensive appendix displays and the switch to two-column main text further change the presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 improves auditability by supplying the detailed results and implementation information missing from the supplied v1, and it better bounds the central claims. These gains are tempered by inconsistencies in the expanded material: Section 3.2's forecast-selection formula conflicts with its state ordering, and Table 17's iTransformer counts total 203 despite the stated 200 scores. Overall reporting and clarity improve, but the new formal justification and numerical documentation still need correction.
